questions.q: According to Siegel, why can stocks be less risky than bonds over long periods?
a: They deliver higher returns after inflation while bonds may lag behind it
They fluctuate less from one year to the next than bonds do
They are guaranteed by the companies that issue them
They pay a fixed rate that automatically rises with inflation
questions.why: Lesson 1 says bonds are calmer but earn less over time and sometimes fail to keep up with inflation.

questions.q: In the 1946 to 2001 comparison, how did bonds perform after inflation?
a: They lost roughly 2.8% a year
They gained roughly 2.8% a year
They matched inflation almost exactly
They beat stocks in most of those years
questions.why: Lesson 1 gives bonds an annual real return of about minus 2.8% over that period, against 6.8% for stocks.

questions.q: What does the noisy market hypothesis say about stock prices?
a: Trading for unrelated reasons pushes prices away from real value
Markets always price every stock at its true worth
Prices move only when a company reports new earnings
Investors behave rationally once they have full information
questions.why: Lesson 2 says tax harvesting, rebalancing and profit taking can move prices away from intrinsic value.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of an ETF according to the summary?
a: It spreads your money across many companies and rides out pullbacks
It guarantees a fixed dividend every year
It lets you buy shares below their fair price
It is reserved for large institutional investors
questions.why: Lesson 3 says an index ETF gives you a slice of every company in the index and withstands market pullbacks.

questions.q: What characterizes a value stock in lesson 3?
a: It trades under its fair price and comes from an overlooked company
It is expected to grow exponentially and usually trades at a premium
It tracks a market index and mirrors its performance
It pays the highest dividend of any stock in its sector
questions.why: Lesson 3 contrasts value stocks with overvalued growth stocks and stresses a price below fair value.
